To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antimicrobial host defence peptide Hp(2- 20) has direct antimicrobial action against H. pylori and immunomodulatory activity on human neutrophils and that the chemokine IL-8 has antimicrobial activity, but lacks the immunomodulatory activities of the intact chemokine.
host defence peptides are multifunctional and that they are able to interact with both microbial and mammalian cells.

the antimicrobial activity of α-helically stabilized host defence peptides is increased, while the immunomodulatory activity is impaired, and that host defence peptides are able to discriminate between viable and apoptotic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional diversity of antimicrobial host defense peptides.
the dual action of host defense peptides.
the dual action of host defense peptides and their role in the innate immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antimicrobial host defence peptide family is functionally diverse and multifaceted, and that the dualism is a prominent feature of this family of molecules.
antimicrobial host defence peptide activity is a function of the α-helix and that this is the common structural feature for all antimicrobial host defence proteins and peptides.
host defence peptides are not only antimicrobials but also immunomodulators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antimicrobial peptides are not only antimicrobial but also immunomodulatory, with the latter activity being sequence-specific.
the dual function of host defence peptides can be explained by the presence of different variants in the same peptide.
antimicrobial host defence molecules are important not only for the innate immune system, but also for the termination of inflammation and for the regulation of the immune system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antimicrobial host defence molecules are multifaceted.

antimicrobial host defence molecules are important not only for their direct action on microbes but also for their indirect immunomodulating effects on human leukocytes and that these two functions may reside in different parts of a single molecule.
the functional dualism of host defence peptides is a prominent characteristic that should be considered in the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
